# 1.2.83 - voice in the Foundry window comes back after a drop, the dead have their own channel, and a question to the GM ends one way

Two stages, built on a second line of work and merged into this one: E19 in full - voice, sound and LiveKit in the Foundry
window, with the voice tile in place of the camera dock - and E18 without its commit C7 - questions to the GM and private cards. A
dropped voice connection now shows a card and comes back by itself; LiveKit runs inside the Foundry window for everyone, and
Foundry's camera dock stays folded while the voice tile is on; a student killed in secret talks with the other dead once the
incident is over, not in the main room; in an Eclipse no player is in voice; and the murder music plays on the Music channel and
leaves the Music volume alone. A question a player waits on says until when it is open and ends one way, a card to the GMs
is ruled once, a private card reaches every player who owns the student and comes back to a reader who was away, and notices to
the whole table stand under the windows. E16 part 1, built on the same line, shipped in 1.2.80 and is not in these notes; E18's
C7 is not in this version (Known gaps). None of it has been tried at a real table yet (Known gaps), and every time measured below is
the test harness's.

## Before installing

1. **Back up the world, and note the version you ran,** so a problem can be traced back.
2. **Voice runs inside the Foundry window for everyone.** A new world setting, *Voice inside the Foundry window for everyone*,
   on by default, holds LiveKit AVClient's separate window or tab off on every browser, the GMs' included, and takes its box out
   of everyone's settings; a change made from a console is put back. A change of the setting takes effect after a reload, and it
   does nothing without LiveKit AV Client enabled. A player who joined voice in its own window joins it in the Foundry window
   after the update (LIVE-E19-06).
3. **While the voice tile is on, Foundry's camera dock is kept folded and no camera opens in a window of its own,** on every
   browser. The two fields are greyed out in Foundry's A/V settings, and a change made anyway is put back a quarter of a second
   later; each player's devices, volumes, mutes, blocks and push-to-talk key stay their own. Each browser keeps how its dock stood
   in a setting nobody is shown, and switching the voice tile off gives it back once, folded or open. Switch the voice tile off
   before you disable the module: a module disabled first gives nothing back (LIVE-E19-07).
4. **The murder music no longer turns the Music volume down.** It plays on the Music channel at the track's own volume. A Music
   volume an earlier version left at 0, after a reload during an incident, is given back when the world loads, in an incident or
   not (LIVE-E19-02).
5. **Private cards a GM's browser kept before this version.** From the first load after the update, each browser asks the
   connected GMs for the words of the private cards to it that it lacks, when its world loads and when a GM comes back; only the
   newest 8 cards of one ask raise a notice. A GM's browser gives back a card it kept before this version only when a GM wrote
   the card, and a line such a card wrote for one player alone comes back in the third person ("Kaito loses 1 Health." in place
   of "You lose 1 Health.").
6. **Settings, keys and texts.** One new setting you see, *Voice inside the Foundry window for everyone*; two more nobody is
   shown (a browser's dock as it stood, and who ruled each card sent to the GMs); no new keybinding. `lang/en.json` goes from 3704
   strings to 3739 and `lang/pl.json` from 4499 to 4534 (37 added and 2 removed in each; 6 reworded in English, 9 in Polish). The
   GM panel's **Reset all voice rooms** is now **Re-send everybody's voice room**, the card of a found body is titled "Body found"
   where it read "A body is discovered", and the hint of *Voice tile instead of the camera dock* now reads "On, the camera dock
   leaves every screen and the number on the voice tile's speaker shows how many others are in your channel, speaking or not.
   Foundry's dock is also kept folded, and no camera opens in a window of its own. Off brings Foundry's camera dock back for
   everyone, folded or open as each browser had it before the tile hid it."

## At the table

### For the GM

- **Re-send everybody's voice room** (GM panel, Between sessions) forgets what each browser was sent and sends every connected
  account its room again at once; with regional voice off it still sends everybody the main room. It answers "Sent {n} people
  their voice rooms again.", and on a GM's browser that is not the primary "Only the primary GM, {name}, can re-send the voice
  rooms. Ask {name}." `game.drpg.reconcileVoice()` now runs at once, as its documentation says.
- **Every connected account has a voice room.** A spectator and a GM holding no Monokuma are each placed in and out of an
  Eclipse and the Class Trial, the main room outside both, where before they kept the Eclipse's room until a reload; a Monocub's
  player is placed in and out of an Eclipse too, outside it in the room its Monocub stands in. An Eclipse that ends by any write
  of the clock, a rewind included, places everybody again.
- **The dead channel.** A victim of an incident keeps the room they died in while the incident runs. Once it closes, the body is
  found, or a living student from outside the incident walks into that room, a death the table has not been told of talks in
  the dead channel, where the dead hear only each other, and a known death goes to the main room; outside an incident this
  happens at once. A living witness joins the room's voice only after the victim's browser says it has moved, or after 1500 ms.
  Monokuma and a Monocub silence nobody, and the Class Trial is unchanged.
- While your browser has not yet read the incident's cast (just after a reload), a player whose student died in this chapter and
  whose page asks for its room is sent there at once, and a living player who walks into a room where a student who died in this chapter lies is sent
  nothing until it has. A student dead since an earlier chapter or season is placed at once.
- `game.drpg.voicePlan()` and the warning on a contested room name the dead channel, where they named the main room.
  `game.drpg.diagnoseVoice()` and `game.drpg.voicePlan()` open with "Proximity Voice Chat is also active." when that module is
  active, also with LiveKit off.
- **In an Eclipse** the GMs share one voice channel, and no player is in voice (For players).
- When a player's browser answers that it could not join its room, the primary GM's browser asks it again after 2 and then 6
  seconds and leaves a third failure to the 60-second pass. The primary's own room is applied last, and a change of ownership,
  of a user's character or role, of the regions or of the Monokuma and Despair pools places the rooms again.
- **The murder music on a GM's browser** holds the room's music at volume 0 and lets it run, because a GM's browser moves the
  table's playlists on; a player's browser pauses it (For players). A track that would not load is asked for again in the next
  incident. The Music tab's note now ends "When a body is found and nothing is mapped to it, the silence stops your own track
  too.", and it does.
- **Breakdown and Wounded** play on every GM's browser and on the browser of each player who owns the student, a co-owner
  included, as the Sound panel says; before, only the primary GM's browser played them. A state put on as the world loads, or
  with the sheet's wand, no longer plays its sound.
- **The Sound window's Effects tab**: Choose, Test and Clear are icons with a tooltip ("Choose a file. In a row that has one
  already, it goes beside it, and one of them is picked each time.", "Play it here, now.", "Empty this row: the event goes
  silent."), each group says "{n} of {total} assigned", "varies" has a legend, and the tab says "Changes here save as you make
  them: this tab has no Apply button." The safeword's row says it is heard whatever the Sound slider says, at Foundry's
  Interface volume, from the first click on the page.
- **One ruling per card.** A press by a GM who is not the primary goes to the primary GM's browser, which takes the card once,
  and the GMs keep a row of who is ruling and who ruled, so a primary that reloads mid-ruling does not free the card. A second GM
  pressing the card reads "{gm} is ruling on this card right now." or "{gm} already ruled on this card.", a card already settled
  reads "This card has already been answered.", and a card its author reopened is not ruled again. These refusals stand in your
  notice history as cards, not as toasts.
- **A question the player waits on** - an Experience or Ultimate Call, a Dynamic action, the statistic a roll lists two of, an
  Observe aimed at a point of interest - says "Open until {time}." on its card: five minutes for a Call, three for the others,
  written by each browser in its own time zone and language, as is the line the card ends with. Your yes or difficulty goes by
  the primary GM's browser, and a Call's or a Dynamic action's card reads "Approved by {name}." or "Answered by {name}." only
  once the player's browser has it; its buttons stay held until the primary rewrites the card.
- If the player stopped waiting, no word came back within eight seconds of the ruling, or the card's time passed, the card ends
  "Nobody answered in time - ask again." for everyone and "The player was no longer waiting." for the GMs, and a Call's yes is
  taken back: nothing is charged. A ruling the player used - a yes their Call was armed on, a difficulty a Dynamic roll was
  thrown on - ends the card as ruled; a difficulty with no word back and no roll ends "Answered by {name} - not confirmed as
  received.", and it stands. A primary GM whose world loads, or which becomes the primary, ends the open cards past their time.
- If the primary GM's browser reloads, or another GM becomes the primary, while a question is open, the player's browser asks
  again, three times at most, and the question keeps its one card; a resend that differs from what the card was posted for is
  refused.
- Your **Reply** in the messenger is the words you type: a reply reading "cancel" is sent, as a player's request is.
- **A private card a player missed**: each GM's browser answers a returning reader from what it holds, to that card's readers
  alone and without the GMs' block, and a line written for that reader comes back as it was written for them.
- **A student two players own**: the private cards to the student, its private rolls, what is heard in its room, the clean-up's
  word to witnesses, an incident's cards and the victim's own words when it closes reach every player who owns the student, and
  a player with Observer or Limited reads none of them. A question one owner asks and waits on lands in that owner's messenger
  thread; the other ruling cards about the student land in one owner's thread.

### For players

- **A dropped voice connection shows a card.** It is titled "Voice disconnected" and says "You are not connected to voice.
  Reconnecting you now; if you still hear nobody in a minute, reload the page (F5)." Your browser joins again by itself about
  1, 5 and 15 seconds after the drop (in the harness 1103, 5101 and 15102 ms, one run), then checks itself every 45 seconds; the
  card goes when voice is back and stays in your notice history, and LiveKit's own disconnect toast is no longer shown. Before,
  the browser read only the room's name, which a drop keeps, and said nothing. When the voice server or another window signed
  in as you closed the connection, the card says "Your voice connection was closed by the voice server or by another window
  signed in as you. Reload this page (F5) to join again." and your browser does not try again.
- **A page that loads** while regional voice is on waits in a room of its own until the primary GM's browser says which room it
  belongs in; with no GM connected it joins the main room.
- **After your character dies in an incident** you stay in the room you died in while the incident runs, then talk in the
  channel of the dead while nobody has been told of your death, and in the main room once it is known. In the channel of the
  dead the voice tile says "Your character is dead: the living do not hear you, and you do not hear them.", and your microphone stays yours to mute
  and unmute.
- **In an Eclipse** your browser leaves voice: nobody hears you and you hear nobody, no "Voice disconnected" card comes, and the
  microphone is grey with the reason under it. When the Eclipse ends, you are back in the room your token stands in, without a
  reload. Before, each player joined a voice room of their own.
- Your voice follows your token through a secret passage into a room where another player stands (LIVE-E19-04).
- **The murder music**, where you take part in the incident, is one track for everybody in it, picked by the incident, on the
  Music channel at your own Music volume, where it was a track picked at random on each browser and played on the Interface
  channel. The room's music is paused and picks up where it stopped when the incident ends. A browser nobody has clicked in since
  it loaded starts the track at the first click, and a track that will not load leaves the room's music playing.
- Breakdown and Wounded of your student play on your browser, and on a co-owner's. A reload during your own turn of an incident
  no longer plays "your turn" at the next change.
- The safeword sound plays whatever your *Sound* slider says, at your Foundry Interface volume, once you have clicked on the
  page since it loaded; the card is what everybody is sure to see.
- **With no GM connected, a question to the GM is not posted**: you are told it was not carried out because "No GM is
  connected.", and what it cost comes back. A Search for something specific is refused before its price and its dice, and when
  the last GM leaves during its roll, the action comes back and the room's search token stays.
- **A question you wait on** says on its card until when it is open ("Open until {time}."), in your own time zone and language.
  If no GM's browser takes a Call or a Dynamic action within eight seconds, you are told at once that it was not carried out
  because "The GM's client did not answer in time." If nobody answers before the card's time, the card ends "Nobody answered in
  time - ask again." and nothing is spent; an answer given after that is not kept. If you reload while you wait, the GM's
  browser ends the card shortly after its time.
- **A request is the words you type**: a request reading "cancel" is sent. A Dynamic action and a Tier 0 item's use refuse an
  empty one with "Nothing was sent - write your request first." and open the window again.
- **Private cards** to your character reach every player who owns it and the GMs, never a player who only observes it, and so do
  its private rolls. If you were away when one was sent, or open the game in another browser, its words come back once a GM is
  connected; a card no GM can fill reads "A private card - its words were sent to another browser and are not kept on the
  server." in place of a dash.

### For everybody

- **Notices to the whole table stand under the windows.** The notice tile goes under Foundry's windows while every card on it is
  a notice to the whole table, and back over them with a card for you alone, a refusal or an objection; a found body's card
  counts as an objection, and the history button alone stands under the windows too (LIVE-E18-03).
- **A notice's bar carries its event's title**, "Notice" only without one; a card that opens with a heading carries it in the bar
  once. The time of day's card says its time once, in the bar, with "Chapter {chapter} · Day {day} · Session {session}" under it.
- **The messenger's bubbles wear the theme**, a card's buttons are at least the small text size and 28 px tall, and a bubble's
  time is written in Foundry's language. In Chromium, on the module's sheets alone, a card's button measured 13 px text and 28 px
  under Monokuma Legacy and 21 px text and 28 px under Stained Glass, where it read 11 px before.
- **The corner** - the launchers, the GM's row, the notice tile and the narrow screen's stack - stands above Foundry's camera dock
  while the dock is shown, under Stained Glass too, and is lifted by nothing while the voice tile hides it.

- No new file: 149 files in `scripts/`, as at 1.2.82.
- **The voice**: `voice.mjs` (`deathVoiceGone`, `olderDeath`, `placeVoices`, `sendInPasses`, `answerWhoAmI`, the tie-break in
  `voiceRowFor`, `createVoiceLedger`, `applyOrder`, `reconcileTrigger`, `eclipseRoomFor`, `resetAllVoice`, `forgetEveryone`,
  `placeName`, `contestedWarning`), `voice-client.mjs` (`landedCorrectly`, `dropCard`, `RECONNECT_MS`, `selfCheck`,

- **The sound**: `music.mjs` (`createMurderOverlay`, `murderTrackFor`, `createRoomHold`, `restoreDuckedMusic`, `nowPlayingHere`,
  `cueGivesWay`), `hud.mjs`, `states.mjs` (`stateSoundsFor`), `sfx.mjs` (`snapshotWorld`, `soundEffectsHtml`) and `config.mjs`.
- **Questions to the GM**: `gm-bridge.mjs` (`callGm`, `holdAsk`, `askMark`, `askAgain`, `sameAsk`, `sweepAskCards`,
  `endAtExpiry`, `expiredOnPrimary`, `receivedOnPrimary`, `endSentOn`, `keepRuling`, `claimOnPrimary`, `claimCard`,
  `sayRefusedHere`, `threadOf`), `bridge-guards.mjs` (`createWaiter`, `RESENDS`), `gm-stores.mjs` (`ruledCardStore`),
  `messenger-app.mjs`, `messenger.mjs`, `action-rolls.mjs` (`performSearch`), `reroll.mjs`, `cleanup.mjs` and `use-items.mjs`.
- **Private cards**: `secret.mjs` (`askForWords`, `answerWordsRequest`, `drawPrivateCard`, `redrawIfDrawn`, `readersLines`),
  `utils.mjs` (`ownerIdsOf` behind `whisperToOwner` and `whisperToOwnerOnly`), `passages-gm.mjs`, `private-rolls.mjs`,
  `murder-rules.mjs` and `incident-store.mjs` (`incidentAudienceIds`).
- **Notices and the messenger's look**: `popup.mjs` (`showPopup` marks each card's kind and hands on the options it does not
  name), `clock.mjs` (`announceTimeOfDay`), `styles/danganronpa.css`, `styles/messenger.css` and `styles/stained-glass.css`.
- **What a player's browser may send**: new bridge actions `ruling.expired` and `ruling.received`, from any known user and acted
  on only for the asker the primary GM holds under that ask, and `dynamic.answer` and `card.claim`, a GM's alone; a new packet
  `secret.request` on the private cards' socket, which each GM answers only to that card's readers. Scenario 30 sends
  `ruling.expired`, `ruling.received`, `card.claim` and `secret.request` from another player's console and reads that none is
  acted on.
- The known leak A9-K3 (a character killed in secret was moved to the main room's voice at the kill) is closed and leaves
  `known-leaks.json`: 8 known leaks, 9 at 1.2.82.
- **Tests**: 46 new numbered tests, R807-R852 (5 in tier 0: R836, R837, R842, R843 and R846; 41 in tier 1); next free R950. 978
  tier-2 titles in `scripts/tests-tier2.mjs`, 956 at 1.2.82.
- The scenario files are still 28; nine change: 75 (the dead channel in E, the Eclipse in B, a drop in H; 37 checks, its bound
  from 90 to 120 s), 13 (the murder music, and the ready path run again mid-incident), 30 (E18's packets from another player's
  console), 33 (C, a call on the GM with no GM; a second check named A17, a clock that runs out), 61 (Y, a handover and the
  primary's reload; CL, two GMs on one card), 62 (T reads the claim's refusal cards), 73 (R, a returning reader), 76 (CO, a
  co-owner and an observer) and 40 (the request window's answer).
- **The manifest's compatibility is unchanged**: Daggerheart `minimum` and `verified` 2.6.5, Foundry `minimum` 14.364 and
  `verified` 14.365.
- The handbooks, in English and Polish: the GM handbook, the player handbook and the player brochure (the dead channel, the
  Eclipse's silence, the drop card and the re-send button, the settings held for every browser, the murder music and the
  safeword's sound, how a question to the GM ends, one ruling per card, a private card a player missed, a student two players
  own).
- Outside the module: `audit/glass-sweep.mjs` checks the corner against a shown and a hidden camera dock at every size;
  `tools/stages.json` gives E18 and E19 `touches: ["sockets"]`, takes E18's tie to E17 away and moves 37 unshipped rows up one
  version, E18 and E19 among them; `docs/dev/R-REGISTRY.md` gains the 46 rows; the audit's section 9.2 gains items
  281 to 294.

## Known gaps

- **LIVE-E19-06** (item 281, not tried yet): on v14 with LiveKit AVClient, a player who had LiveKit's separate window on joins
  voice in the Foundry window, sees no Join window and no meet.livekit.io tab, and has no such box in the settings; the A/V Config
  fields are greyed out, whose v14 names are not read here; switching the setting off asks for a reload and gives the box back.
- **LIVE-E19-07** (item 282, not tried yet): with the voice tile on, everybody's dock folded and no camera in a window, the
  others heard, also after F5, and a dock opened from a console folded again with the devices, volumes, mutes, blocks and
  push-to-talk kept.
- **LIVE-E19-01** (item 283, not tried yet): a real drop - one "Voice disconnected" card, no LiveKit toast, the joins after 1, 5
  and 15 s and the 45-second check, the card gone on return; the same account in a second window; which disconnect reasons
  livekit-client gives, and whether LiveKit AVClient joins again by itself.
- **LIVE-E19-02** (item 284, not tried yet): a player's F5 during an incident leaves the Music slider where it stood, the murder
  track plays on after the first click, and the room's music comes back after; a volume an older version parked is given back.
- **LIVE-E19-03** (item 285, not tried yet): the murder track on the Music channel, the same for everybody in one incident, the
  room's music paused for a player and held at 0 for a GM; a track that will not load; a player's F5 before the first click;
  another room track started during the incident.
- **LIVE-E19-04** (item 286, not tried yet): a crossing through a tunnel, a teleport and a displacement into a room where another
  player stands, and how long until they hear each other; after an Eclipse, a spectator and a GM with no Monokuma in the main
  room.
- **LIVE-E19-05** (item 287, not tried yet): the dead channel on a real LiveKit - nobody alive hears the dead, the witness's wait,
  the primary GM's F5, a victim's reload while the cast loads, and a console's own `game.webrtc.connect()`.
- **LIVE-E19-08** (item 288, not tried yet): an Eclipse with two players, a spectator and two GMs - every player out of voice with
  no card and no join for minutes, the GMs in one room, everybody back after it without a reload.
- **LIVE-E19-09** (item 289, not tried yet): Proximity Voice Chat active beside the voice rooms - the diagnosis's first line, and

- **LIVE-E19-10** (item 290, not tried yet): the corner and the notice tile over a real camera dock, both themes, at 1920x1080,

- **LIVE-E18-04** (item 291, not tried yet): what v14's chat log does with an old private card it has not drawn when that card is

- **LIVE-E18-03** (item 292, not tried yet): the notice tile under and over real windows, a vote over a public card, the bar's
  title and its letters' height under Stained Glass, and the request card's buttons, in both themes.
- **LIVE-E18-01** (item 293, not tried yet): a Hope Call Experience, a Dynamic action and a project proposal with one GM and two
  players in both languages, the card's time for a player in another time zone, the five-minute end, no GM connected, and a
  co-owner and an observer.
- **LIVE-E18-02** (item 294, not tried yet): the primary GM's F5 mid-question, an Assistant GM made primary, two GMs on one card,
  and v14's order of a reloading GM's events.
- **E18's C7 is not in this version**: Frisk's ask does not yet go by the road the other questions to the GM take, and a
  sabotage sent again does not yet answer with its first result (E18-31, E18-32). It waits for E36.
- On a GM's browser the room's music is held at volume 0 for the incident, not paused, so a GM's playlists keep moving.
- The 1500 ms a witness waits for the victim is the design's number, not measured at a table. The Mastermind killed and a GM's
  own character that is not a Monokuma are not tested as cases of their own.
- While the primary GM's browser holds no cast, a living player in a kept victim's room is sent nothing and stays where their
  page was, for the whole incident if the GMs' store never loads. A death of the running chapter that is not the incident's is
  still kept in that time.
- With no GM connected when a page loads, it joins the main room; a dead student who loads then is heard there until a GM
  connects.
- A browser whose LiveKit never comes up (its server down at load) shows the drop card and joins again every 45 seconds, also
  with regional voice off; not measured at a table.
- An Eclipse ended by a rewind is read through the clock's write only; no rewind is run.
- A dock that stands only under the left half of the screen lifts nothing, so the notice tile stays over it; under Stained Glass
  the room tile in its "notes" place stands on the screen's edge and can cover a shown dock beside the notice tile.
- Whether Foundry's own sync, restarting a paused room track, is heard for a moment before the player's browser pauses it again
  is not measured.
- The Music channel following the Music slider, a missing file failing quietly and a track waiting for the first click are
  read in Foundry 14's types, not heard; the scenario's reload is the ready path run again, not a reload; two GMs and a reload
  before the first click are not tested apart.
- Breakdown and Wounded on two GMs' and a player's browsers are driven on plain objects, not heard; the turn sound's quiet start
  after a reload is read in the source.
- The Effects tab's two columns and icons are not measured in a browser; its groups do not fold, and a row has no "saved" mark.
- The pick on a statistic's card is sent by the GM who pressed it and written "Answered by" at the press: a press after the
  player's clock ran out, but before the primary heard of it, is written as ruled though the player was told there was no
  answer. The statistic's and the Observe's asks have no eight-second clock, unlike a Call and a Dynamic action.
- The primary's end of a card at its time still settles a card another GM is ruling on, and that GM's ruling then settles it
  again.
- A GM that connects between a Dynamic difficulty sent on and its card's end holds no ruling for that card, so as primary it
  reads an older card's (read in the code, not driven).
- The Dynamic difficulty window names the character the player's request named, while the card names the sheet's.
- A GM's press on a first card whose mark the primary could not read is refused once a resend has its own card, and that first
  card stays open until its time.
- A GM that only received a veiled card with no thread, or only a ruling's words of a player's card, holds no readers for it
  and gives nothing back; the GM that posted it does. A GM that got a card's words from another GM before this version, or by a
  reader's ask, answers in the third person. A card a player wrote, whose words no GM held, is not filled from the player's
  own browser: it reads the private card line above.
- An ask of more than 100 cards, and only the newest 8 raising a notice, are read in the code, not driven.
- An old card a GM rewrites far up the log is still handed to each reader's chat log to draw again (LIVE-E18-04).
- The day's summary and the messenger's cards count as cards for you alone and keep the notice tile over the windows.
- With a second owner, the ruling cards about the student other than the waited questions (a Search for something specific, an
  Analyze hint, a Tier 0 item, a project) and the notes a ruling posts after them go to one owner's thread; checks that a sender
  is the student's owner still compare with one owner, so a co-owner is refused there; a private roll with a co-owner is not
  written private when it is created (LIVE-E33-03).
- A GM leaving during the room's search token's own write still leaves the token taken; an Analyze hint's refund on a call that
  was not posted is not driven; an Assistant GM alone counts as a connected GM (read in the code).
- A card a GM deleted mid-question, both primaries' F5 within one question, and two tabs of one player are not driven or
  measured; v14's order of a GM's connection against its ready packet is not measured (LIVE-E30-05).
- Known leaks whose stages have not shipped are unchanged.
